`Date.now = jest.fn()` throws the real `Date.now` away. Unless you save it and put it back yourself, every test that runs afterwards gets the mock. `spyOn(Date, "now")` remembers the original, so `mockRestore()` or `mock.restore()` brings it back.

`--fix-suggestions` rewrites `obj.save = jest.fn()` to `jest.spyOn(obj, 'save').mockImplementation()`. The `.mockImplementation()` is there because a spy calls the original function until you give it an implementation.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import { beforeEach, jest } from "bun:test";

beforeEach(() => {
  Date.now = jest.fn(() => 1700000000000);
  console.warn = jest.fn();
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { afterEach, beforeEach, mock, spyOn } from "bun:test";

beforeEach(() => {
  spyOn(Date, "now").mockImplementation(() => 1700000000000);
  spyOn(console, "warn").mockImplementation(() => {});
});

afterEach(() => {
  mock.restore();
});
```

A mock that is stored in a variable or written in an object literal replaces nothing, so it is not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { jest } from "bun:test";

const onSave = jest.fn();
const logger = { warn: jest.fn() };
```

The rule only looks for `jest.fn()` and `vi.fn()`. It does not report `mock()`, which has the same problem:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { mock } from "bun:test";

Date.now = mock(() => 1700000000000);
```
